correctness.rationale: With N=q², Fourier transforming the output in modulation is unitary and splits the lift by lag h=z−w. On the h band the map is sqrt(N) times translation correlation with k_h(z)=g(z)g(z−h). For a lag with nonzero first coordinate, planarity makes k_h a delta so all N singular values of that band are q. Nonzero vertical lag gives a zero band. At zero lag, the Fourier transform over translations is diagonal up to signs with coefficients q times the character sums of the graph. These sums have magnitudes q at the trivial character, zero at (r,0) for r≠0, and sqrt(q) at (r,s) for s≠0 by expanding the square and using the permutation of differences. This verifies the full spectrum and rank under the actual counting normalization, and the kernel is arbitrary within-fibre off-diagonal matrices plus a diagonal constant on each fibre with constants summing to zero. For ss*−tt* in the kernel, two nonzero cross-fibres force the same fibre support and reciprocal scalars up to phase; a third produces unimodular scalars all equal. In the two-fibre case a nontrivial reciprocal rescaling must act on flat profiles, and preservation of total energy gives the unique unequal-amplitude swap. In the one-fibre case the same support preserves each individual modulus, and a different fibre is possible only with full flat profiles of equal energy. Total energy is measured, so zero is unique. These checks use arbitrary complex signals and any planar f, not just a quadratic prime-field example.
residual_risks: Packaged examples cover only q=3,5,7 for x²; the proof, rather than those scripts, supplies prime-power and every-planar-function coverage. Full measurements and the stated window normalization are essential.

evidence: The Gabor lift in Fourier coordinates is multiplication by window ambiguity on matrix bands. The graph of a planar function is an (n,n,n,1) relative difference set relative to the vertical subgroup, with converse. This fixes all translated intersection counts and the three character magnitude strata of the unshifted indicator.
Split-quadratic projector spectra concern graphs on F^r×F^r×F, r≥2, and Gold-graph spectra concern characteristic two; the inspected records do not claim the frozen nonlinear classification.

evidence: The cubic-chirp text states that the cross-class products, classwise nonzero-lag periodic autocorrelations and total energy are necessary and sufficient data for equality. In planar-graph coordinates the necessary and sufficient data are cross-fibre products, each squared-modulus profile modulo constants, and total energy.

A unitary length-p discrete Fourier transform in every block conjugates each cross-block by fixed invertible matrices. Wiener–Khinchin identifies all nonzero-lag autocorrelations precisely with the centred Fourier squared-modulus profile, and preserves total energy.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Thus for p≥5 the data equivalence is exact after a change of coordinates. The three-block rigidity and the swap on flat profiles are the same theorem in those coordinates. The one-block classification also follows directly from the source's sufficient data: same-block Fourier moduli are fixed by total energy, and switching blocks requires all measured nonzero-lag autocorrelations to vanish. The cubic theorem did not state that last case, but its sufficient-data lemma implies it. This comparison does not assert within-day precedence.

originality.rationale: A distinct nonlinear phase-fibre classification as the central contribution is not established. The same-day cubic-chirp record provides necessary and sufficient data which, under a unitary Fourier transform within each block, are exactly the planar-window data when q=p≥5 is prime. This is an equivalence of the measurement fibres, not just a similar two-case description: the other record's proof data imply the one-fibre clause as well, and the spectra agree after window normalization. Its same-day date does not determine priority, and its theorem does not literally cover all odd prime powers or all planar windows. What is left beyond the demonstrably equivalent prime-case normal form is an application to the larger planar family: the requisite band magnitudes are direct outputs of the classical relative-difference-set identities and standard Gabor multiplier, and the nonlinear step then repeats the same block algebra with q instead of p. No materially distinct nonlinear result is established in the frozen finding beyond that extension; this is not a claim of chronological priority or that an earlier paper prints the entire theorem verbatim.
residual_risks: The two Nov. 8 records cannot be temporally ordered on the evidence used. The cubic-chirp theorem does not literally cover q=3 or nonprime q. The decision rests on the demonstrated data equivalence plus the character of the extension, not a claim of proven earlier publication.

value.rationale: Independently of priority, identifying exactly what a natural family of relative-difference-set windows can and cannot recover is scientifically useful. The result separates failure of arbitrary-matrix tomography from support-free phase uniqueness on a large class of rank-one signals, and characterizes the exceptional ambiguities rather than just producing a rank defect. The evaluation in terms of omitted matrix directions identifies which signal structure matters.
residual_risks: No inverse stability or subsampling guarantee is established. Usefulness of the application to a natural window family does not establish manuscript originality.
